details:
Project Details – SARScope: Earth’s Radar Explorer

Overview
SARScope is an interactive educational web platform that makes Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery easier to understand and explore. I developed it independently for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, under the team name Orbital Rhythm. It makes complex radar remote-sensing concepts accessible to students, beginners and anyone curious about Earth observation.

What it does
The platform presents SAR imagery, polarization concepts and satellite data through a clear visual interface. It includes real HHHH and HVHV imagery extracted from a NASA-processed NISAR Level-2 Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance (GCOV) product, so users can see how different polarizations reveal different aspects of Earth’s surface. Interactive educational demonstrations explain SAR concepts further. These are clearly labelled as simulated and kept separate from real observations.

Benefit and impact
Rather than relying on lengthy technical explanations, SARScope lets users learn by exploring. It aims to spark curiosity about satellite technology, raise awareness of remote sensing and open Earth observation to a wider audience.

Technology
SARScope is built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and React, using imagery and metadata extracted from the NISAR GCOV product. AI-assisted development tools were used during development.

Creativity and design
SARScope pairs real satellite data with an interactive learning experience. It was designed for usability, clarity, scientific accuracy and accessibility, with particular care to separate real observations from simulations and to explain technical ideas in beginner-friendly terms.
